myStory.role: A specialised ADHD coach certified, neurodivergent, multilingual, and a mum to two brilliantly wired kids.
myStory.diagnosis: I was diagnosed late, like many adults, and I'm still figuring shit out, personally and professionally.
myStory.honesty: I'm not here with all the answers.
myStory.mission: I'm here to walk beside you, ask good questions, and help you explore what actually works for your brain and your life.

whoIsFor.title: Who is this for?
whoIsFor.intro: This space is for those who are ready to try something new, to break free from rigid molds and find what truly works for their brain. If you're:
whoIsFor.audience1: A late-diagnosed ADHD adventurer who's still figuring out your flavor
whoIsFor.audience2: Someone who loves an ADHD-er and wants to understand them at the core of their being
whoIsFor.audience3: An entrepreneur or artist whose creativity feels trapped behind the walls of structure
whoIsFor.audience4: A parent who's been holding the weight of neurodivergence without guidance
whoIsFor.conclusion: Then, this enchanted space is for you.
whoIsFor.goal1: Stop trying to fit yourself into a mold — it's like trying to fit a square peg into a round hole
whoIsFor.goal2: Take control without losing yourself to rejection sensitivity — it's about finding strategies that respect your energy
whoIsFor.goal3: Let go of perfection — real life doesn't come with a perfect recipe, but it's yours to shape
whoIsFor.goal4: Build a life that works with your brain — think of it as fine-tuning your engine, like a chef perfecting their dish

simulator.section1_lead: You have a race car engine...
simulator.section1_desc: Welcome to the ADHD Simulator. Scroll down to experience the ride.
simulator.section2_p1: Here is a very mundane task. Imagine this is a tax form, or a long email from HR, or the instructions for a board game you don't really want to play. Notice how your scroll wheel feels heavy? That's the friction. Your brain refuses to supply the dopamine needed to process this low-stimulation information.
simulator.section2_p2: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit. Sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur.
simulator.section2_p3: Are you skimming this? Of course you are. It's painful to read word for word. Why is the scroll so slow? Why can't we just skip to the fun part?
simulator.section3_fact: Did you know penguins utilize projectile poo?
simulator.section3_outro: Did you feel the scroll speed up? Your brain loves this. It's easy, it's colorful, it's irrelevant.
simulator.section4_p1: But it's not all chaos. When the stars align, or the deadline is 5 minutes away, or you find something *truly* fascinating...
simulator.section4_p2b: The friction disappears. The background noise fades. You become a machine.
simulator.section4_hint: Try the "ACTIVATE HYPERFOCUS" button at the top right to see what clarity feels like.

assessment.title: Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-v1.1)
assessment.instructions: Please answer the questions below based on how you have felt and conducted yourself over the past 6 months.

questions.q1: How often do you have trouble wrapping up the final details of a project, once the challenging parts have been done?
questions.q2: How often do you have difficulty getting things in order when you have to do a task that requires organization?
questions.q3: How often do you have problems remembering appointments or obligations?
questions.q4: When you have a task that requires a lot of thought, how often do you avoid or delay getting started?
questions.q5: How often do you fidget or squirm with your hands or feet when you have to sit down for a long time?
questions.q6: How often do you feel overly active and compelled to do things, like you were driven by a motor?
questions.q7: How often do you make careless mistakes when you have to work on a boring or difficult project?
questions.q8: How often do you have difficulty keeping your attention when you are doing boring or repetitive work?
questions.q9: How often do you have difficulty concentrating on what people say to you, even when they are speaking to you directly?
questions.q10: How often do you misplace or have difficulty finding things at home or at work?
questions.q11: How often are you distracted by activity or noise around you?
questions.q12: How often do you leave your seat in meetings or other situations in which you are expected to remain seated?
questions.q13: How often do you feel restless or fidgety?
questions.q14: How often do you have difficulty unwinding and relaxing when you have time to yourself?
questions.q15: How often do you find yourself talking too much when you are in social situations?
questions.q16: When you're in a conversation, how often do you find yourself finishing the sentences of the people you are talking to, before they can finish them themselves?
questions.q17: How often do you have difficulty waiting your turn in situations when turn taking is required?
questions.q18: How often do you interrupt others when they are busy?

assessment.errorIncomplete: Please answer all questions to proceed.
